statement.p: A biologist has been observing a trees height. 12 months into the observation, the tree was 14.58 feet tall. 18 months into the observation, the tree was 16.32 feet tall.

Let x be the number of months passed since the observations started, and let y be the trees height at that time, in feet. Use a linear equation to model the trees height as the number of months pass.

To find the slope, we need two points on the line. We have been given that (12,14.58) and (18,16.32) are points on the linear model, so we can use the slope formula:

This lines slope is 0.29. This implies that the tree is growing by 0.29 feet each month.

So now we have that y=0.29(x-x_0)+y_0. We can either use (x_0,y_0)=(12,14.58) or (x_0,y_0)=(18,16.32) to get {y = 0.29\mathopen{}\left(x-12\right)+14.58\hbox{ or }y = 0.29\mathopen{}\left(x-18\right)+16.32}.
